summary: A scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Kara studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Gyula Németh and Lajos Ligeti. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and Indiana University (Professor, 1993–2022).
Hashimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Join Saeki and at the University of Tokyo (~1922–1925). He later served as head at Yakushiji from 1939 to 1967.
Gé Mang Khenchen Yönten Gyatso was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shechen Gyaltsab.

Colas is an Indologist affiliated with the CNRS, where he was attested as Directeur de recherche in 2004 and Senior Fellow in 2009. He was also attested as CNRS Directeur de recherche at EHESS in 2012.

Fussman worked in Indology, history and archaeology, and linguistics. After studying at the École Normale Supérieure (~1960–1965), he served as Professeur at the Collège de France beginning in 1984, succeeding Jean Filliozat, and headed a CNRS unit (attested 1994).

Bethlenfalvy was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Lajos Ligeti, and later held appointments at the University of Delhi (1970), Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Vienna as visiting professor (2007–2008).

An Indologist and linguist, Liebert earned his doctorate at the University of Gothenburg in 1949, studying under Frisk, Holmer, and Wikander. He taught at Lund and Uppsala before serving as professor at the University of Gothenburg from 1955 to 1982.

A scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, von Selle studied at Berlin, Kiel, and Göttingen (Dr. phil.). He held librarian posts at Göttingen and served as professor and deputy library director at Königsberg (~1938–1945).
Blamberger held a post at the University of Kassel (~1992–1995) and was appointed Chair in German Philology at the University of Cologne around 1995.

Grönbold worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Bavarian State Library (~1974–2008), serving as Head of the South Asia Department (~1980–1988) and head of the Oriental Section (~1988–2008).

Working in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Schweiger studied at the Vienna University of Economics and Business and under Gert Klingenschmitt. He served as ordentlicher Universitätsprofessor at the Vienna University of Economics and Business from 1974 to 2009.

Linguist H. Craig Melchert studied at Michigan State University, the Defense Language Institute, the National Cryptologic School, and Harvard University. He held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1978–2007) and UCLA (2007–2015).

Sankalia was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at University College London (~1934–1936) and served as an archaeologist at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (1945–1946).

Narahari was an Indologist who earned his BA Hons. at Mysore and an M.Litt. at Madras, studying under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1944, he was attested as a Research Assistant at Adyar Library and Research Fellow at Madras.
De Graaf was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Leiden University (~1919–1926) and under Poerbatjaraka between 1927 and 1930.
Kikuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who was attested in 1966 as a research student at the University of Delhi studying under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale.
Aiyangar was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who held positions in the Kannaḍa/Canarese Department at the University of Madras, attested in 1938 and 1957.
Rao is an Indologist, philosopher, and linguist. He held a post at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and was attested in 2012 as a Professor at the University of Mysore.
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Haeju Sunim was a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and was attested as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Dongguk University in 1999.

A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, Hu-von Hinüber completed her MA at Peking University under Kemo Jin and studied under Zhongxin Jiang. She held posts at the University of Vienna (1996) and University of Freiburg (Director, 2010).
